text:
When all the ants have left the clock

and at last the door of solitude opens,

death

will no longer find me.


It will look for me among the trees, crazed

by the silence of one thing after another.

It will not find me on the unraveling plateau,

feeling it at the fountain of a rose.


I am splitting the fruit of insomnia

with the hand knifed by chance.

And the house is open in such a way

that death will no longer find me.


And it must look for me above the trees and among the clouds.

(Fruit and color the voice will set ablaze!)

And I cannot wait for it: I have a rendezvous

with life, by the lights of a song.


Footsteps are heard—very far away?…—there is still

time to escape.

For night to raise its stars,

a deep sound of shadows fell over the sea.


Now blood crashes against the heart.

Night falls so brightly that I can undress.

Thus, when death comes looking for me,

it will find only my clothes.

translation.title: When All the Ants Have Left the Clock...
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the recurrent pursuit by death and the final reversal. The evident source typo ‘sobe’ is read as ‘sobre’ in the line about shadows falling over the sea.
